chunks: “Al-Wadhah” means “al-khunfasa’ (dung-beetle).” In this sentence, he refers to al-Hajjaj, and there is a narration concerning him and “al-khunfasa’” which is not the place to mention it here.

key_terms.الْحَجَّاجِ: Al-Hajjaj (referring to al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi)
key_terms.الْوَذَحَةُ: Al-Wadhah (a specific term used in the text)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-Wadhah' refer to in Nahj al-Balagha and who does it allude to?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid al-Sharif identifies 'al-Wadhah' as the beetle (al-khunfasa), employing it as a metaphorical epithet for the Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, known for his harsh rule. This interpretation aligns with the Shia tradition of linking specific prophetic or Imami predictions to historical figures, though the full hadith establishing this link is reserved for a different context within the text.
